# The Torvig radio outage of 12 March — harbour office report

*Invented material. See the README of the demo project.*

This is an account of one night, written up by the Torvig harbour office the
morning after. It is not a rule and it was never meant to become one.

## What happened

The mainland radio link went down at 19:40 on 12 March and stayed down until
the following midday. Torvig fell back on the signal mast at once. Fenmouth
answered, Ovray Cove did not: the cove has no mast of its own and is read from
the Bellhorn mast, which nobody was standing under after dark.

## What the office did

1. Red was hoisted over blue at 19:55 — harbour closed, pilot requested — and
   the pilot boat came out from Fenmouth ninety minutes later.
2. The office kept a paper log of every hoist, because the radio log writes
   itself and the flag log does not.
3. At 22:10 a boat off Ovray Cove hoisted white on the Bellhorn mast. Torvig
   read it at first light, not at 22:10, and the doctor reached the cove eleven
   hours after she was asked for.

## What the office wrote down afterwards

The gap was not in the code. Every flag hoisted that night meant what the code
says it means. The gap was that a flag has to be *looked at*, and after dark
nobody was looking at Bellhorn. The office asked the tide office in Fenmouth
for a lamp on that mast; whether one was ever fitted is not recorded here.
